positive.prompt: Audit the agent context in this repo — what should live in AGENTS.md vs a skill?
Our skills library has grown messy and agents keep ignoring the conventions. Review it.
Which of our instruction files and rules are actually loaded, and what do they cost?

negative.prompt: My agent forgot the project conventions mid-session, fix its context
Review this pull request for bugs

evals.prompt: Audit the agent context in this repository and produce the full report.
evals.expected_output: An eight-section report whose inventory, load map and rubric findings come from the validator, with each judgment finding tied to a rubric line or a named context-engineering anti-pattern.
expectations: scripts/audit_context.py is executed against the repo rather than the inventory being assembled by hand
The report contains all eight sections from references/report-template.md, in order
The always-tier token budget is stated as a number and includes every skill's frontmatter description, not only the root instruction files
Every finding cites a rubric line (R1-R8) or a named anti-pattern from the context-engineering skill
Findings that could not be evidenced appear under Unverified rather than in the findings tables

evals.prompt: A skill in this repo links to a shared doc with a path that does not resolve. Find it and say where the content belongs.
evals.expected_output: The broken links identified from validator output, with a placement decision taken on the relocation ladder rather than an ad-hoc fix.
expectations: The unresolved links are reported with file and line, taken from the validator rather than by reading each file
The response distinguishes a genuinely broken link from a path that resolves only in a consuming repo
A destination rung from the relocation ladder is named for the shared content, with the rung's test applied
The fix is concrete (a specific path or a specific move), not 'consider revising'

evals.prompt: Cut the always-loaded context in this repo and prove the cut did not break anything.
evals.expected_output: A measured before/after always-tier budget plus an eval suite with baselines recorded before the change.
expectations: Before and after always-tier token numbers are both measured with the validator, not estimated
At least three eval cases exist and each targets a specific finding from the report
Baselines are recorded on the pre-change tree, before any file is moved
Cases that pass both before and after the change are reported as proving nothing rather than as successes
Any regression is reported rather than omitted

evals.prompt: The context-engineering skill is not installed here. Audit the repo anyway.
evals.expected_output: A rubric-only audit that declares the missing source in the header instead of reconstructing it.
expectations: The absence of the context-engineering skill is stated in the report header
The operating model is not reconstructed from memory or invented
The rubric half of the audit is still completed in full
Findings that would have required the missing source are listed under Unverified
